sentences.text: JUSTICE
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 750/2020 registered at Police Station Raj Park, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/354/376/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all other proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Naveen Kumar and Investigating Officer (IO) from Police Station Raj Park, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 12.02.2009.
From the wedlock, one male child and one girl child were born.

It is stated that due to certain misunderstanding and differences, respondent no. 2 had lodged a complaint vide FIR No. 750/2020 for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/354/376/34 of IPC at Police Station Raj Park, Delhi against the petitioners.
Thereafter, parties had amicably settled their disputes vide Settlement Deed dated 24.02.2023 before Ghaziabad Family Court.

5. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any Ved Prakash And Ors vs State And Anr on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76146527/
1 pressure, coercion or threat.

sentences.text: It is also stated by respondent No. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Ghaziabad Family Court, Delhi.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor children as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.

6. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

7. It is stated that petitioner no. 1 has already paid a sum of Rs. 3,50,000/- towards full and final settlement to respondent no. 2.
8.
Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the entire amount, as per settlement.
and has no objection, if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 750/2020 registered at Police Station Raj Park, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/354/ 376/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of 12.
The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 21, 2023/ns
